correctness.rationale: The structure determinant is (up to sign) \(1-(-1)^m a\), so all admissible algebras are perfect. Strong connectivity and a direct ideal argument give simplicity. Perfectness makes automorphisms monomial; graph symmetries are exactly rotations. The coefficient equations force a \(C_M\) diagonal kernel and admit a rotation lift with \(\phi^m=d^{ur}\), where \(u\) is the inverse of \(2\) modulo \(M\). Smith normal form gives \(C_g\times C_{mM/g}\), and the necessary-and-sufficient condition \(\gcd(m,M)\mid r\) governs splitting. Exact finite-field instances, including characteristic two, were recomputed in the bundled checkers; finite computations do not stand in for the universal proof.

value.rationale: Question 33 of the 2026 survey asks which perfect evolution algebras have split diagonal/graph automorphism sequences. A uniform infinite family of simple perfect algebras realizes both split and nonsplit extensions and distinguishes them by an exact divisibility test, yielding cyclic nonsplit examples for every odd prime and an explicit full automorphism-group calculation. This supplies a structurally motivated parameterwise answer beyond one isolated \(C_9\) example without claiming the full general problem is solved.
